evals.prompt: We need to grant a small one-time credit top-up when a user completes onboarding, on top of their normal tier credit grant. Add the entitlement/meter for it.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes a new meter needs a shared-kernel + packages/contracts entry first (api-contract-change), then implements the grant transactionally in apps/api/src/modules/billing/internal/, ensures the credit ledger invariant (balance = sum of entries, never negative, oldest-expiring consumed first) holds, and adds a lifecycle-matrix test in apps/api/src/modules/billing/tests/.
assertions: The agent either finds the meter/entitlement name already registered in packages/shared-kernel or explicitly stops to request the registry + contract addition before writing billing code
The credit grant is applied transactionally and the agent's report states which invariant (balance = sum of entries, never negative) the new test proves
A test exists in apps/api/src/modules/billing/tests/ and the agent's report names `just test billing` as the command run
No RevenueCat SDK import appears in apps/api/src/modules/billing/** — only a port implemented in apps/api/src/platform/

evals.prompt: RevenueCat just sent us a duplicate CANCELLATION webhook for the same subscription (looks like a retry) and it downgraded the user's entitlement twice, double-logging a billing event. Fix the webhook handler.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats this as a regression: reproduces the double-processing with a webhook-replay test, confirms the fix uses event-id dedup via the idempotency-keys table so a duplicate event is a no-op, reruns the webhook idempotency test suite to show green, and flags that this touches a webhook handler so `security-privacy-review` is needed before PR.
assertions: The agent's report includes the actual failing test output captured before the fix (duplicate event caused a double downgrade / double log), not a paraphrase
The fix implements or corrects idempotency-key dedup rather than adding an ad hoc duplicate check outside that mechanism
The agent explicitly states that `security-privacy-review` is required before this webhook-handler PR merges
The agent reruns the billing webhook tests after the fix and pastes the passing output

evals.prompt: Product wants to A/B test a $2 lower price point for the Plus monthly tier to see if it improves conversion.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes this is a price/tier experiment, not an entitlement change, and either declines to implement it under this skill (stating it is a product/pricing decision recorded as a doc 12 hypothesis, and that server-driven offering experiments are P13-T14's PostHog flag-assignment work with the explicit guardrail that experiment schema cannot touch entitlement enforcement) or scopes the task narrowly to the entitlement-safe seam only.
assertions: The agent's response states that price/tier experiments are out of scope for this skill and points to the doc 12 hypothesis framing
If any code is touched, it does not modify entitlement-enforcement logic — only offering/experiment configuration, consistent with P13-T14's guardrail
The agent never presents the new price as validated or claims a conversion result it did not measure
